Regime analysts and the media theorize that the West threatens Russia’s survival, that it wants to control its natural resources and even eliminate most of the population in order to rule the elite.

At the recent Valdai Conference, Putin openly accused Europe of the protracted war in Ukraine, ignoring Russia’s role in the aggression and annexation of Crimea. Analysts recall that the relationship between Russia and Europe was previously significantly different. Since the 1990s, Russia has had partnerships with the EU and was negotiating membership in NATO. Agreements such as the “Partnership for Modernization,” cooperation within the Russia-NATO Council, and economic projects such as Nord Stream have demonstrated Moscow’s willingness to be part of the European political and economic space.

However, over the past few decades, Putin has rejected the idea of ​​rapprochement with Europe, moving towards an imperial, Greater Russia policy. Fears of the “Europeanization” of Russia and the strengthening of liberal democratic principles, which could threaten his authority, have strengthened conservative and nationalist tendencies in the Kremlin.
This ideological factor is also part of the conflict with Ukraine, which, unlike Russia, has accepted democratic standards and political pluralism, which has further alarmed the Kremlin.

are more than just military reconnaissance. They are intended to cause uncertainty and panic, but also to test the reactions of European countries and NATO. There is currently a debate about who is responsible for neutralizing unknown drones – the police or the army – and how to implement the law governing the shooting down of aerial objects. Reisner emphasizes that such incidents force governments to act concretely and prepare procedures, because otherwise there is a risk of losing control over the country and critical infrastructure.

Before Putin turned Russia towards a more aggressive policy, relations with the West were significantly closer. As early as 2010, there were plans for a single European economic space with a common visa regime and security system. Partnership agreements with the EU and military-political cooperation with NATO were maintained until the annexation of Crimea in 2014. Russia was also a member of the G8, and significant investments in the Nord Stream 1 and 2 gas pipelines secured its strategic position in energy supplies.

However, Putin gradually abandoned European integration and focused on domestic control and imperial expansion. Fears of democratization and the West's insistence on human rights and media freedom contributed to his turn to conservative ideologues such as Vladislav Surkov and Alexander Dugin, which strengthened the Kremlin's authoritarian course.

These meetings serve to spread the ideas of radical movements and further destabilize the European political space.
